The skeleton width (d) and height (δ) of the honeycomb structure determine the alignment effect and the filling content of conductive microcoils.
The inscribed circle radius of the hexagonal structural unit (r) is limited by the processing capacity and the efficiency of honeycomb mold.
The parameters of the honeycomb structure were initially designed with d = 0.2 mm, δ = 0.4 mm, and r = 1 mm.
The conductive microcoils/ethanol mixture (approximately 1 wt %) was added dropwise to the mold heated to 60 °C.
The rapid evaporation of ethanol drives the movement of the liquid film edge toward the microgroove.
The desired conductive networks composed of ordered conductive microcoils were constructed until every microgroove was full.
The sintering temperature range investigated was 300 °C, 350 °C, and 400 °C.
The copper coating just slightly melted at 300 °C, and the nanojunctions between adjacent conductive microcoils did not obviously change.
Irregular nanocracks were formed due to the excessive melting of the copper coating at 400 °C.
The stretching test system consisted of a mechanically uniaxial stretching platform and stepper motor.
The EMI shielding materials can withstand up to 100% strain without significant degradation.
Liquid metal was used to secure the accuracy of the resistance value during the cyclic strain test.
The source meter (Keithley 2602B) with two electrodes was used to test the resistance of the EMI shielding materials.
The microhoneycomb molds with different microgroove widths (0.15, 0.2, and 0.3 mm) were used to investigate the alignment effect.
The three-dimensional scanning morphologies of the microhoneycomb molds were used to visualize the alignment effect.
